chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said during the standing: 'Raise yourselves from the bottom of Bait Uraynah.' And he said: 'The people of al-Arak have no Hajj.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The basis of inference from these two is that the Prophet (peace be upon him) invalidated the Hajj of anyone who left the boundary of Arafat, even if he was standing. Had standing in it not been obligatory, he would not have invalidated the Hajj of someone who stood outside its boundary; rather, he would have permitted him to not stand at all.

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْأَرَكَ: The people of al-Arak (a specific location)
key_terms.بَطْنِ عُرَنَةَ: The bottom/valley of Uraynah (a specific location)

ai.seo_question: What is the evidence for the obligation of standing at Arafat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar underscores the juridical necessity of the specific location of Arafat for Hajj validity, citing the Prophet’s dismissal of those who remained at al-Arak as evidence that mere presence outside the boundary is insufficient. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan’s analysis highlights that if standing outside were permissible, the Prophet would not have invalidated their Hajj; thus, the ritual is contingent upon fulfilling the condition of standing within the prescribed limits. This reinforces the Shia scholarly view that the spatial definition of Arafat is a core pillar (rukn) rather than a mere recommended act.
